On a Friday in mid-July, a delivery truck carrying forty-eight twenty-litre jugs of liquid chlorinating solution entered the Mirelle Bay Pool Supply yard. While a forklift was carrying the pallet to the covered dock, the load fell and split open in the loading yard. Multiple jugs burst open, causing the liquid to spread toward a drain at the low edge of the yard. Warehouse staff promptly placed sand bags around the drain before emergency responders arrived. Two warehouse workers walked away from the spill upwind within a minute of the fall. Warehouse staff and the driver provided differing accounts regarding the exact cause of the fall, attributing it variously to uneven stacking, shifting loads, or a broken section of yard paving.

The Tessin Fire Service logged the call and arrived shortly thereafter. Firefighters wearing breathing apparatus righted the surviving jugs and moved them under a tarpaulin at the dock, and washed the remaining liquid into a temporary holding bund. A licensed waste contractor collected the contained liquid the following morning. Meanwhile, the business park air monitor registered chlorine above its alarm threshold, peaking before eventually dropping back down below the threshold later that afternoon.

Sources: Warehouse supervisor Neve Aldersgate's statement, Business Park Air Monitor Record, Driver Oskar Penhallow's statement, Tessin Fire Service Incident Report, Mirelle Bay Pool Supply Yard Gate Log, Yard Camera Archive
